one_line: A deterministic job-shop scheduling workspace shared by humans and agents.
what_it_does: Users express scheduling constraints, an agent edits the model through WebMCP, and a browser MILP solver computes, validates, and explains schedules with audit history.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools and canonical shared state make agent-authored constraints, deterministic solving, stale-state detection, and auditability materially more reliable than UI driving; the solver, rather than the LLM, owns correctness.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies typed constraint tools, a real HiGHS MILP solver, stale schedule detection, infeasibility explanations, and a shared audit timeline.
The intended workflow combines human, agent, and solver actions on one canonical model.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent end-to-end scheduling product and frame-sheet evidence is listed, but no transcript and only claimed rather than observed completion limit confidence.
execution_evidence: Description names scheduling, Gantt inspection, constraints, solving, stale-state handling, and audit history as one workflow.
Three submitted video frame sheets are listed; no transcript is provided.
impact_rationale: Manufacturing and operations users have a concrete high-value need for schedules that respect interacting constraints and can be audited.
impact_evidence: Pitch and description identify machine downtime, deadlines, dependencies, overrides, and infeasibility as real scheduling problems.
Deterministic validation directly addresses the risk of an LLM inventing an invalid schedule.
creativity_rationale: The human-agent-solver collaboration and canonical audit state are a thoughtful, ambitious interaction model beyond a generic chat wrapper.
creativity_evidence: The concept explicitly separates natural-language intent, structured agent actions, and deterministic optimization.
Stale-model detection and deterministic infeasibility explanations deepen the concept.
usability_note: The stated workflow is structured and understandable, though visual evidence was not independently readable in this review.
red_flags: No transcript and limited independently inspectable evidence; execution claims are not fully verifiable.
standouts: Solver-backed correctness instead of trusting an LLM.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP leverage and credible operational value, with enough coherent evidence to advance despite incomplete video verification.

leverage_evidence: Extracted about text is predominantly generic Devpost navigation and contains no substantiated WebMCP workflow.

execution_evidence: No video frame sheets submitted.

impact_evidence: No coherent product description is present in the extracted submission text.
creativity_rationale: There is insufficient project-specific material to identify a novel concept or interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Packet contains no usable concept evidence beyond the pitch 'AI'.
usability_note: No product workflow can be assessed from the packet.
red_flags: Submission text appears to be navigation boilerplate.
Product identity and WebMCP implementation are unsubstantiated.
advance_reason: The packet lacks enough project evidence to evaluate quality or WebMCP contribution.

one_line: A shared incident console where an on-call human and an external agent investigate together.
what_it_does: Sightline exposes incident metrics, traces, logs, deploy correlation, evidence pinning, rollback proposals, and postmortem drafting through WebMCP while preserving human approval for rollback.
leverage_rationale: The agent reads and changes the live investigative state through explicit tools, enabling a shared screen and precise handoff that ordinary UI driving or a separate chat cannot replicate comparably reliably.
leverage_evidence: Nine tools are claimed, including get_current_view, metrics/traces/logs queries, evidence pinning, rollback proposal, and postmortem drafting.
Description emphasizes shared state, visible attribution, exact arguments/results, and human-only rollback approval.
execution_rationale: The product concept is unusually coherent and the submitted screenshot/frame evidence shows a real incident-console surface; end-to-end behavior remains claimed because there is no transcript.
execution_evidence: Screenshot visibly shows INC-4417, checkout latency charts, service list, deployment timeline, agent investigation, and rollback-related decision UI.
Three frame sheets are listed and the pitch says every call visibly changes the screen.
impact_rationale: Incident responders have a specific, high-stakes need for fast, shared, auditable diagnosis and controlled mitigation.
impact_evidence: Concrete checkout latency incident with metrics, traces, logs, deployments, and rollback is described.
Human approval boundary addresses operational risk while preserving agent speed.
creativity_rationale: Replacing the sidebar chatbot with a shared operational console and explicit handoff state is a fresh, deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: No chat panel; agent and human operate the same screen and state.
Visible attribution and exact call/result inspection make collaboration part of the product.
usability_note: The incident-console layout appears information-dense but purpose-built, with clear operational panes and human approval boundaries.
red_flags: No public repository and no transcript; tool invocation claims are not fully independently verified.
standouts: Human-only rollback approval and inspectable tool calls.
advance_reason: Exceptional fit between WebMCP and the product's core collaboration model, with credible visual product evidence and high operational value.

one_line: A risk, permission, and discovery layer for WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: AIC audits WebMCP applications and provides registration and agent.json metadata that makes tool risk, authorization, confirmation, and completion verification explicit and enforceable.
leverage_rationale: The product targets a real protocol gap: structured risk metadata and registration enforcement change whether agents can safely discover and invoke consequential tools, rather than merely automating UI actions.
leverage_evidence: Census claims 75 tools, 49 mutating, with zero enforceable risk signals.
Package reportedly refuses consequential registration without authorization, confirmation metadata, and a verifier, and publishes /.well-known/agent.json.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a focused implementation and visible catalog/demo packaging, but the screenshot is packaging plus an embedded demo preview and lacks a transcript or repository execution proof.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly identifies the project and embedded demo context.
Description specifies a scan command, real document.modelContext registration, and machine-readable discovery output.
impact_rationale: Safe discovery and authorization are foundational needs for an ecosystem where agents can invoke mutating web actions.
impact_evidence: Measured examples include order submission, booking, and deletion tools lacking enforceable risk semantics.
The proposed layer addresses authorization, confirmation, and completion verification before consequential calls.
creativity_rationale: The project turns empirical ecosystem auditing into a protocol-level safety and discovery layer, a strong and timely angle.
creativity_evidence: Census-driven diagnosis of concrete WebMCP patterns and API divergence.
Combines CI-testable registration policy with /.well-known/agent.json semantics.
usability_note: The metadata and refusal model appears developer-oriented and actionable, though implementation ergonomics are not demonstrated end-to-end.
red_flags: Claims about every public app and protocol semantics are not independently verified in the packet.
No frame sheets were successfully inspectable here beyond packaging evidence.
standouts: Concrete ecosystem census rather than generic safety claims.
Enforceable consequential-tool registration and machine-readable discovery.
advance_reason: Addresses a high-leverage infrastructure gap with credible specific implementation and ecosystem impact.

one_line: An agent-native document and evidence workspace for tax work.
what_it_does: Kodi exposes document discovery, evidence retrieval, governed reasoning, citations, and reversible document actions to external agents while retaining a visible tax-document library.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to canonical evidence, revisions, and reversible actions materially improves reliability over manually moving tax evidence between a UI and separate AI.
leverage_evidence: Seven tools cover discovery, evidence access, reasoning, and reversible actions.
Description claims search, exact canonical retrieval, citation/warning-aware answers, revision verification, trash/restore, and continued workflow state.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a detailed, internally consistent workflow with 13 documents, trash/restore, revisions, and multiple completed capabilities; frame sheets and ten gallery images are listed, though no transcript is provided.
execution_evidence: Claims seven capabilities complete successfully across search, retrieval, reasoning, rename, trash, restore, and revision verification.
Visible library and side-by-side external-agent framing are described; three frame sheets are listed.
impact_rationale: Tax filers and preparers have a concrete evidence-management and governed-answer problem where provenance and warnings matter.
impact_evidence: Targeted Kenyan sole-proprietor tax workflow uses utility-expense evidence and citations.
Canonical document access and warnings address the risk of unsupported tax answers.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent-native shared evidence state and reversible document operations to tax is a strong domain-specific synthesis, though the underlying workspace category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: External AI can continue a tax objective by inspecting evidence and acting on the same library.
Restorable actions and revision verification are integrated into the agent workflow.
usability_note: Document states, citations, warnings, and reversible actions suggest a careful workflow for a high-consequence domain.
red_flags: Project explicitly predated the challenge; eligibility depends on challenge rules for extending an existing product.
No transcript, so claimed agent invocation sequence is not fully observable.
standouts: Governed canonical evidence with citations and warnings.
Reversible agent actions with revision verification.
advance_reason: High impact and strong execution evidence; flag pre-existing origin for eligibility review.

one_line: A trip itinerary board where a visible agent edits shared plans under human locks.
what_it_does: Waypoint lets a human and agent add, update, remove, and reorder itinerary activities, while deterministic conflict and budget checks and locked activities constrain agent changes.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central to the shared, visible, lock-aware board: structured tools enforce user decisions and return post-change computed state, unlike a separate chat or brittle UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Eight tools operate on the same itinerary board and enforce locked activities.
Every mutation returns schedule, conflicts, budget deltas, and actionable hints; shared activity feed logs human and agent actions.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete central workflow including reset, conflict recurrence, agent repair, lock preservation, and deterministic checks; frame sheets are listed, but no transcript is supplied.
execution_evidence: Demo sequence claims a human resets the board, agent detects and fixes a conflict, and locked lunch remains untouched.
Implementation details specify React/TypeScript, eight tools, JSON schemas, and deterministic returns.
impact_rationale: Travel planners have a clear need to coordinate constraints, budgets, and changing preferences without losing human control.
impact_evidence: The product directly handles itinerary conflicts, budgets, ordering, and user-locked decisions.
Visible beside-you collaboration addresses the gap between hidden booking agents and manual planning.
creativity_rationale: The lock-enforced, same-board human-agent planning interaction is a memorable and well-developed application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Locked lunch is enforced at the tool-contract level, not merely suggested in text.
App-computed math and shared feed make corrections and accountability part of the interaction.
usability_note: The lock model, deterministic feedback, and visible activity feed are strong usability safeguards for collaborative planning.
red_flags: No transcript and frame sheets were not fully inspectable due to review-tool rate limits.
standouts: Deterministic conflict/budget feedback after each agent mutation.
advance_reason: Excellent WebMCP leverage with a clear, demonstrably useful shared-state planning workflow.

one_line: A human-approved spatial repair rehearsal for unsafe temporary-clinic layouts.
what_it_does: Rehearse lets an agent inspect a layout, run deterministic accessibility-style spatial checks, stage ghost geometry, and propose a patch that a person must approve and verify.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools plus revision/hash binding create a safe shared state and prevent stale or autonomous application of spatial repairs; generic UI automation would be substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Five tools perform state reading, spatial checks, staging, application of an approved patch, and verification.
Apply requires matching visible proposal, approved hash, and base revision; autonomous approval is impossible.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a complete failure-and-recovery sequence with deterministic routing, stale rejection, re-planning, atomic apply, and receipt verification, though no frame sheets were submitted.
execution_evidence: Detailed stale-proposal sequence: lock reception, increment revision, reject old patch, reread, replan, approve, verify.
Implementation claims bounded-grid A*, stable tie-breaking, atomic commit, and SHA-256 receipt.
impact_rationale: Temporary clinics and other time-pressured layouts have a concrete need to detect blocked routes and repair them without silently violating human decisions.
impact_evidence: Description identifies blocked routes, pinch points, inaccessible destinations, and obstructions.
Human approval and post-commit verification are appropriate for spatial safety planning.
creativity_rationale: The proposal-as-ghost-geometry plus revision-bound human approval is an original and carefully constrained interaction model.
creativity_evidence: A stale proposal is deliberately demonstrated as a first-class failure mode.
Hash-bound, lock-aware patches and receipts extend beyond a generic layout editor.
usability_note: Ghost previews, explicit approval, and verification receipts provide a clear and safe operational flow.
red_flags: No frame sheets or transcript submitted; execution is based on detailed claims rather than visual observation.
standouts: Human-only approval and deterministic post-commit receipt.
advance_reason: Strong safety-aware interaction and credible implementation detail make this a compelling agent-native planning tool.

one_line: A structured creative canvas where agents compose with spatial awareness alongside humans.
what_it_does: Auxweave represents text, images, shapes, frames, layouts, and relationships as structured scene objects so agents can create and refine designs without reasoning over raw pixels.
leverage_rationale: Structured scene geometry and higher-level spatial tools improve agent precision over coordinate-level UI automation, though the same design outcomes remain possible with other structured APIs.
leverage_evidence: Description says agents manipulate typed canvas objects and spatial relationships.
Canvas tracks dimensions, object geometry, and relationships to reduce collisions and incoherent layouts.
execution_rationale: The concept and architecture are coherent, but no frame sheets, video, or concrete end-to-end result evidence are supplied.
execution_evidence: About text describes a scene representation and spatial logic.
No video frame sheets submitted and no visible completion sequence is available.
impact_rationale: Designers and creative teams have a real need for agent assistance that preserves layout hierarchy and reduces destructive edits, though demonstrated value is thin.
impact_evidence: Problem statement identifies collisions, text overlap, and broken hierarchy in agent-generated designs.
Target users can combine human composition with structured agent refinement.
creativity_rationale: Treating a canvas as spatially semantic shared state, rather than a pixel surface, is a fresh and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Concept asks the canvas to help agents understand space.
Higher-level objects and relationships are central rather than a cosmetic WebMCP wrapper.
usability_note: The intended spatial model is promising, but the packet does not show enough UI or completed designs to assess actual usability.
red_flags: No frame sheets, video, or concrete visual output submitted.
Access model and implementation completeness are unclear.
standouts: Semantic spatial scene model for agent-assisted design.
advance_reason: Creative concept is strong, but execution and product evidence are too thin for advancement at this stage.

one_line: A persistent intelligence dashboard where humans and agents organize evolving web information.
what_it_does: OpenBento combines WatchBots, live news and social cards, notes, columns, financial cards, and AI assistance in persistent canvases shared by human and agent actions.
leverage_rationale: Shared persistent canvas state and semantic card/watchbot actions are useful WebMCP improvements over a separate chat, but the packet does not demonstrate how much structured precision changes outcomes.
leverage_evidence: Description emphasizes shared canvases, cards, WatchBots, and dashboard state.
Agents can operate explicit application actions rather than screenshots or brittle coordinates.
execution_rationale: The product scope is broad and internally coherent, but no frame sheets, video, or concrete completed workflow evidence are provided.
execution_evidence: About text enumerates persistent dashboard objects and WatchBot behavior.
No submitted video frame sheets.
impact_rationale: Researchers, analysts, and information-heavy users have a recognizable need for persistent monitoring and curation rather than ephemeral chat answers.
impact_evidence: WatchBots continuously surface discoveries while users preserve important cards on a dashboard.
The described product combines live feeds with durable organization.
creativity_rationale: The persistent live-feed-to-curated-dashboard model is a fresh synthesis, although adjacent intelligence dashboards and research workspaces exist.
creativity_evidence: Cards can be pulled from a live WatchBot stream into a persistent dashboard.
Human and agent share the same evolving workspace rather than a one-shot answer channel.
usability_note: The dashboard model is understandable, but the large surface area and lack of UI evidence make usability uncertain.
red_flags: Very broad scope with no demonstrated central workflow.
standouts: Persistent WatchBot streams combined with curated dashboard state.
advance_reason: Promising concept and audience, but evidence is too thin to credit execution or WebMCP impact confidently.

one_line: A 3D room planner that lets humans and agents rearrange furniture and check accessibility together.
what_it_does: RoomCraft provides a live 3D room, manual furniture editing, and WebMCP tools for reading layout, moving objects, measuring gaps, checking clearance, and responding to natural-language scenarios.
leverage_rationale: Agents operate a structured live 3D scene, reason over geometry and clearance, and respond to human edits; this is far more reliable than screenshot-based browser driving for spatial tasks.
leverage_evidence: Description says the agent reads live layout, moves real objects, measures gaps, and checks clearance inside the page.
Shared canvas and activity panel expose real calls; the agent can detect a manually introduced blocked door and fix it.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete interactive 3D workflow with furniture editing, scenario changes, route checking, and activity logging; frame sheets are listed, though no transcript is supplied.
execution_evidence: Demo sequence includes dinner-party rearrangement, wheelchair route checking, deliberate sofa obstruction, diagnosis, and fix.
Project claims a complete 3D planner with 18 always-available tools plus selected-object controls.
impact_rationale: Home planners and people considering accessibility have a concrete need to understand spatial arrangements and clearance before acting.
impact_evidence: Examples cover hosting guests, wheelchair access, blocked balcony door, and natural iterative room changes.
Deterministic clearance checks turn visual planning into actionable feedback.
creativity_rationale: Combining conversational agent collaboration with a manipulable 3D spatial scene and accessibility reasoning is memorable and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Agent uses room state rather than a screenshot and can react to human drag edits.
The same room supports manual, conversational, and mixed improvisational planning.
usability_note: Natural-language scenarios, direct manipulation, visible activity logging, and red/green route feedback form a compelling mixed-mode experience.
red_flags: No transcript; exact agent calls are inferred from the detailed packet description and listed frames.
standouts: Human edits and agent accessibility checks share one 3D state.
advance_reason: High WebMCP indispensability, clear visual product workflow, and strong memorable impact for spatial planning.
